title: Covering by Hamming balls: a counting bound
statement: Let $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $\mathrm{Cand}$ be finite sets, and assign to each candidate $c \in \mathrm{Cand}$ a function $\mathrm{center}(c) \colon \alpha \to \beta$. For a radius $e \in \bbn$, write the Hamming ball of radius $e$ about $c$ for the set of functions $f \colon \alpha \to \beta$ that differ from $\mathrm{center}(c)$ in at most $e$ coordinates, that is, with $\abs{\{a \in \alpha : \mathrm{center}(c)(a) \neq f(a)\}} \le e$. Suppose that every such ball contains at most $B$ functions, and that every $f \colon \alpha \to \beta$ lies in the ball about at least one candidate. Then \[ \abs{\{\text{functions } \alpha \to \beta\}} \le \abs{\mathrm{Cand}} \cdot B. \]
hypotheses_covered: center assigns to each candidate a function α → β
e and B are natural numbers
each Hamming ball of radius e about a center contains at most B functions
every function α → β lies within Hamming distance e of some center
